$notes: Reference ranges are published anthropometric / cephalometric norms for adults, stated as (mean, sd) per sex where the literature gives them, otherwise as a typical range converted to a mean and sd under a normal assumption. Every entry cites its source key in references.json.
Where the literature is pooled (no sex split), the same values are used for both sexes and `pooled` is true.
`direction` says which way a deviation is scored: 'toward_mean' (both tails penalised), 'higher_better', 'lower_better', or 'none' (displayed only, never scored).
reliability_tier is PROVISIONAL until the test-retest harness (eng doc, Telemetry) measures it. Provisional tiers were set from the landmark source's known precision. The harness overrides this file.
score_weight_cap is derived from evidence_grade per the eng doc table and is recomputed by the engine; it is stored here only so the file is self-describing.
`modifiable` marks metrics a tier-1/2 rule can actually move (soft tissue, skin). 'Most improvable' is chosen only among these; bone metrics are never called improvable.

metrics.name: Facial width-to-height ratio
metrics.definition: Bizygomatic width divided by the distance from the midpoint of the brow line to the top of the upper lip.
metrics.plain: How wide your face is relative to its height between brow and lip.
metrics.note: Geniole et al. 2015 meta-analysis: higher fWHR associated with LOWER rated attractiveness (r = -0.26). Shown with the 'Research points the other way' badge. Zero score weight.

metrics.name: Canthal tilt
metrics.definition: Angle between the intercanthal axis (medial to lateral canthus) and the horizontal, averaged across both eyes. Positive = lateral canthus higher.
metrics.plain: The upward angle of your eyes from the inner corner to the outer corner.
metrics.note: Population variation is documented by ancestry; pooled reference used with a wider band when ancestry is unknown. Roll gate ±2° matters: a 2° roll error is a full SD.

metrics.name: Interocular distance ratio
metrics.definition: Intercanthal distance divided by bizygomatic width.
metrics.plain: How far apart your eyes sit relative to the width of your face.

metrics.name: Eye aspect ratio
metrics.definition: Palpebral fissure height divided by fissure width, averaged across both eyes.
metrics.plain: How tall your eye opening is relative to its width.
metrics.note: Highly expression-dependent; neutral-expression gate is required. Displayed only.

metrics.name: Eye width to spacing
metrics.definition: Mean palpebral fissure width divided by intercanthal distance. The 'one eye width between the eyes' rule gives 1.0.
metrics.plain: Whether the gap between your eyes is about one eye wide.

metrics.name: Upper third share
metrics.definition: Trichion-to-glabella height divided by total trichion-to-menton height.
metrics.plain: Forehead height as a share of your whole face.
metrics.note: Trichion is unreliable with hairstyle and hairline recession; provisional tier C, qualitative only.

metrics.name: Middle third share
metrics.definition: Glabella-to-subnasale height divided by total trichion-to-menton height.
metrics.plain: Nose-length region as a share of your whole face.

metrics.name: Lower third share
metrics.definition: Subnasale-to-menton height divided by total trichion-to-menton height.
metrics.plain: Nose-base-to-chin as a share of your whole face.

metrics.name: Lower third split
metrics.definition: Subnasale-to-stomion divided by subnasale-to-menton. Classical ideal 1:2 gives 0.333.
metrics.plain: Where your mouth sits between nose and chin.

metrics.name: Midface ratio
metrics.definition: Interpupillary distance divided by the vertical distance from the interpupillary line to the top of the upper lip.
metrics.plain: Eye spacing relative to the height of your midface.
metrics.note: Community convention; no clinical norm located. Displayed with the community badge, weight cap 0.02.

metrics.name: Nasal base width
metrics.definition: Alar base width divided by intercanthal distance. The classical rule says the alar base equals the intercanthal distance (1.0).
metrics.plain: How wide your nose base is relative to your eye spacing.
metrics.note: Most distance-sensitive metric in the set (Ward et al. 2018: ~30% wider at 12 in than 5 ft). The distance gate exists for this.

metrics.name: Nose length
metrics.definition: Nasion-to-subnasale divided by total face height.
metrics.plain: How long your nose is relative to your face.

metrics.name: Mouth to nose width
metrics.definition: Mouth width divided by alar base width.
metrics.plain: How wide your mouth is relative to your nose.

metrics.name: Mouth to pupil spacing
metrics.definition: Mouth width divided by interpupillary distance.
metrics.plain: Whether your mouth corners line up under your pupils.

metrics.name: Upper to lower lip ratio
metrics.definition: Upper vermilion height divided by lower vermilion height.
metrics.plain: The fullness of your upper lip relative to your lower lip.
metrics.note: Popenko et al. 2017 (JAMA Facial Plast Surg): 1:2 ratio rated most attractive in women. Male norm less studied; shown with wider band.

metrics.name: Jaw to cheek width
metrics.definition: Bigonial width divided by bizygomatic width.
metrics.plain: How wide your jaw is relative to your cheekbones.
metrics.note: Gonion is a soft-tissue estimate from the frontal view and is adiposity-sensitive; the adiposity head is a covariate.

metrics.name: Chin width
metrics.definition: Soft-tissue chin width at the mentolabial level divided by mouth width.
metrics.plain: How wide your chin is relative to your mouth.

metrics.name: Forehead to cheek width
metrics.definition: Minimum frontal (bitemporal) width divided by bizygomatic width.
metrics.plain: How wide your forehead is relative to your cheekbones.

metrics.name: Facial index
metrics.definition: Morphological face height (nasion to menton) divided by bizygomatic width.
metrics.plain: How long your face is relative to its width.

metrics.name: Bilateral symmetry
metrics.definition: 1 minus the mean normalised displacement between each paired landmark and its mirror across the fitted midsagittal plane, in the de-rotated frame.
metrics.plain: How closely the left and right halves of your face mirror each other.
metrics.note: Reference is provisional pending the harness: lighting asymmetry inflates measured asymmetry, which is why the luma gate exists.

metrics.name: Brow height
metrics.definition: Vertical distance from lower brow edge to upper lid crease, divided by palpebral fissure width, averaged.
metrics.plain: How close your brows sit to your eyes.

metrics.name: Philtrum length
metrics.definition: Subnasale-to-labrale-superius divided by lower-face height (subnasale to menton).
metrics.plain: The distance between your nose and upper lip, relative to your lower face.

metrics.name: Nasofrontal angle
metrics.definition: Angle at nasion between the glabella tangent and the nasal dorsum tangent.
metrics.plain: The angle where your forehead meets your nose bridge.

metrics.name: Nasolabial angle
metrics.definition: Angle at subnasale between the columella tangent and the upper lip tangent.
metrics.plain: The angle between the base of your nose and your upper lip.
metrics.note: Armijo et al. 2012 (Arch Facial Plast Surg): ideal 93.4–98.5° men, 95.5–100.1° women by rater survey.

metrics.name: Nasal tip projection
metrics.definition: Goode ratio: perpendicular from alar crease to pronasale divided by nasion-to-pronasale length.
metrics.plain: How far your nose tip projects from your face.

metrics.name: Facial convexity
metrics.definition: Angle at subnasale formed by glabella-subnasale and subnasale-pogonion (soft tissue). 180 = straight.
metrics.plain: Whether your profile is straight, convex or concave from forehead to chin.
metrics.note: Legan & Burstone 1980: 12° ± 4° angle of convexity, expressed here as 168° ± 4–5°.

metrics.name: Mentolabial angle
metrics.definition: Angle at the mentolabial sulcus between the lower lip tangent and the chin tangent.
metrics.plain: The angle of the fold between your lower lip and chin.

metrics.name: Cervicomental angle
metrics.definition: Angle at the cervical point between the submental line and the anterior neck line.
metrics.plain: How sharply your jaw turns into your neck.
metrics.note: Ellenbogen & Karlin 1980: aesthetically ideal 105–120°. Strongly adiposity-driven, hence the strongest evidence for a modifiable metric.

metrics.name: Chin to E-line
metrics.definition: Signed perpendicular distance from soft-tissue pogonion to the Ricketts E-line (pronasale to pogonion is the line; measured here as lower-lip-to-E-line as the clinical proxy). Negative = behind the line.
metrics.plain: Where your chin sits relative to a line from nose tip to chin.
metrics.note: Requires metric scale; on a rear-camera profile capture, iris-based scale is the fallback. Provisional tier C until spike 4.

metrics.name: Gonial angle
metrics.definition: Soft-tissue approximation of the angle at gonion between the ramus tangent and the mandibular border tangent.
metrics.plain: The angle at the back corner of your jaw.
metrics.note: Skeletal norms (≈120–130°) are not directly comparable to the soft-tissue estimate; ramus tangent is often obscured by hair and ear. Qualitative only until the harness says otherwise.

metrics.name: Ramus length
metrics.definition: Soft-tissue tragus-to-gonion divided by gonion-to-menton.
metrics.plain: The height of the back of your jaw relative to its length.

metrics.name: Forehead slope
metrics.definition: Angle of the trichion–glabella line from the vertical (perpendicular to Frankfort horizontal).
metrics.plain: How much your forehead slopes back.

metrics.name: Skin evenness
metrics.definition: Appearance-head output in [0, 1]: 1 = uniform tone and texture across the face region after lighting normalisation. Categorised as high / moderate / low.
metrics.plain: How even your skin tone and texture are.
metrics.note: Fink, Grammer & Matts 2006 and related work: skin colour homogeneity is among the stronger, fastest-changing predictors of rated attractiveness. Requires the stricter skin lighting gate. v1 source: core/appearance/skin.py — illumination-normalised texture + chroma spread inside a cheek/forehead mask; a spread, not a level, so no skin-tone preference by construction. Residual ≈0.05 luma dependence documented; measured in the week-9 fairness smoke.

metrics.name: Facial adiposity
metrics.definition: Appearance-head output in [0, 1] estimating perceived facial adiposity, fused with soft-tissue jaw width and cervicomental angle when available. Categorised as low / moderate / high.
metrics.plain: How much soft tissue sits over your facial structure.
metrics.note: Coetzee et al. 2009 and Re & Rule: perceived facial adiposity is a reliable predictor of rated attractiveness and health. Lower-better is applied only down to the reference mean minus 1 SD; below that the term is flat, so the engine never rewards very low adiposity. v1 source: core/appearance/adiposity.py — geometric proxy from the mesh (lower-face width, cheek fullness, submental bulge). Labelled as a proxy in the metric card.

metrics.name: Hairline
metrics.definition: Norwood-Hamilton stage estimate (1–7) from the frontal view; shown as a category only.
metrics.plain: Where your hairline sits and whether it is receding.
metrics.note: Never scored. Exists to trigger the tier-3 referral rule (minoxidil/finasteride named, never dosed).

metrics.name: Facial hair
metrics.definition: Category: clean-shaven / stubble / short beard / full beard. Covariate for jaw and chin metrics; never scored.
metrics.plain: Whether facial hair is covering your jaw and chin lines.
metrics.note: When beard is present, jaw/chin soft-tissue metrics have their confidence multiplied by 0.8 and the card says so.
